title: High-entropy alloy catalysts for electrochemical CO2 reduction
insights: Cu-rich sites can activate CO2 and stabilize COOH* intermediates.
Ag and Pd can tune CO binding strength and improve CO selectivity.
High-entropy mixing provides diverse local coordination environments.

title: Machine learning screening of multimetallic catalysts for CO2 electroreduction
insights: COOH* formation energy and H* adsorption energy are useful descriptors for CO2RR selectivity.
XGBoost can provide a fast first-pass ranking before expensive DFT calculations.
Weak H* binding helps suppress the competing hydrogen evolution reaction.

title: DFT descriptors for CO production on transition-metal surfaces
insights: Moderate COOH* stabilization is important for the first proton-electron transfer step.
Overly strong CO* binding may block active sites.
The balance between COOH* formation and H* adsorption can guide catalyst selection.

title: Stability design principles for high-entropy electrocatalysts
insights: Configurational entropy can improve phase stability in multicomponent catalysts.
Surface segregation should be checked because active surface composition may differ from bulk composition.
AIMD can be used after initial DFT screening to verify thermal stability.
